purpose: Content architecture for the always-accessible educational help/explanation system (task section 11). Definitions + contextual help + 'why did the result change?' logic. NOT a UI implementation.

global_help_panel.what_is_profile_B: A topical celastrol (tripterine) nanoparticle delivery scenario - a lipid nanocarrier applied to skin, studied for cutaneous melanoma.
global_help_panel.celastrol: A poorly-water-soluble, chemically-reactive triterpenoid from Tripterygium wilfordii; encapsulated to improve solubility/stability.
global_help_panel.NLC: Nanostructured lipid carrier - a nanoparticle of mixed solid+liquid lipids that carries the drug.
global_help_panel.formulation_preset: A complete, experimentally-defined formulation package. You pick a preset, not individual ingredients, because the literature only supports specific tested combinations.
global_help_panel.why_not_free_combine: Most excipient combinations have never been tested; letting users mix them would invent untested formulations.
global_help_panel.particle_size: Nanoparticle diameter (here ~85-90 nm). Affects transport and uptake.
global_help_panel.PDI: Polydispersity index - how uniform the sizes are (lower = more uniform).
global_help_panel.zeta_potential: Surface charge in mV; influences stability and cell/skin interaction.
global_help_panel.cationic_neutral_anionic: Positive / near-zero / negative surface charge configurations - here each also uses a different lipid, so charge is not the only difference.
global_help_panel.encapsulation_efficiency: Fraction of drug trapped in the carrier.
global_help_panel.apparent_release: Release measured through a dialysis membrane, where membrane transport and true carrier release cannot be fully separated.
global_help_panel.permeation: Drug crossing skin (measured ex vivo on rat skin here).
global_help_panel.precipitation: Released drug coming out of solution as solid - a RISK for poorly-soluble celastrol, with no known precise timing.
global_help_panel.aggregation: Nanoparticles clumping - not measured over time for this formulation.
global_help_panel.degradation: Chemical breakdown of celastrol - known generally, not timed here.
global_help_panel.what_is_modeled: release, skin permeation, and (optionally) uptake compartments.
global_help_panel.what_is_visual_only: surrounding cells, ECM, vasculature, precise precipitation/aggregation timing.
global_help_panel.evidence_limitations: single study, rat skin (not human), no independent validation, surface charge confounded with lipid identity.

why_did_the_result_change.release_differs: Different surface configurations released celastrol at different rates - but the configurations also differ in lipid composition, so this is an observed association, not a pure charge effect.
why_did_the_result_change.permeation_differs: Cationic showed the highest skin permeation; note the cationic formulation also uses a different lipid (stearylamine/IPM) - do not attribute the difference to charge alone.
why_did_the_result_change.uptake_differs: Charge-dependent uptake observed in HaCaT/B16BL6; same confound caveat.
why_did_the_result_change.lag_time_differs: Small differences in Franz lag time between configurations (0.42-0.52 h).
why_did_the_result_change.stability_differs: Not measured over time - the tool must NOT claim a stability difference it did not observe.
why_did_the_result_change.precipitation_risk_differs: Governed by released-drug solubility, not directly measured per configuration - present as qualitative risk only.
why_did_the_result_change.mandatory_wording: This difference was observed between formulations that differed in BOTH surface charge and lipid composition; it should not be interpreted as a pure isolated charge effect.
